data.description:
## Goal / user story

As a proxy operator, I want empty upstream 200 responses to be retried more times, so that transient gateway hiccups self-heal instead of exhausting the whole fallback chain.

## Context / evidence

- 2026-09-10 proxy logs: `opencode-go-2` (`muse-spark-1.3-contributor`) returned an empty 200 (`saw_tool_calls=False saw_reasoning=False`), retried once after 2s, still empty, then the whole chain exhausted (opencode-go-3 usage-limited, deepseek 402).
- Current config (`proxy/config.yaml`): `upstream_empty_retry_max_attempts: 1`, `upstream_empty_retry_base_delay_seconds: 2.0` — only 2 total attempts.
- One extra retry (~3s delay) would likely have recovered if the hiccup was transient.

## Scope

Config-only change in `proxy/config.yaml`:

```yaml
upstream_empty_retry_max_attempts: 3
upstream_empty_retry_base_delay_seconds: 3.0
```

Verify both streaming (`proxy_remote.py` stream generator) and non-streaming (`_handle_remote_non_streaming`) paths pick up the new values.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

1. `proxy/config.yaml` sets `upstream_empty_retry_max_attempts: 3` and `upstream_empty_retry_base_delay_seconds: 3.0`.
2. A transient empty upstream response (empty on first 2 attempts, content on 3rd) resolves without falling back to the next provider.
3. A persistently empty upstream still falls back after retries are exhausted (no infinite retry).
4. Relevant proxy test suites pass.
data.title: Increase empty-response retry attempts to 3 with 3s delay

data.description:
## Goal / user story

As a proxy operator, I want the adaptive upstream timeout to account for Responses-API (`input`) bodies, so that `api: openai-responses` providers (opencode-go Muse) do not hit a spurious 60s ReadTimeout on large contexts.

## Context / evidence

- 2026-09-10 live session `herdr-1789053754-372301-1821`: repeated exact-60s `Upstream ReadTimeout` on `opencode-go` (`muse-spark-1.3-contributor`): 17:16:47→17:17:47, 17:18:49→17:19:49, 17:51:08→17:52:08.
- Root cause chain: `proxy_remote.py:proxy_to_remote` translates chat `messages` → Responses `input` (line ~801-806), THEN calls `_compute_request_timeout(server_config, body_json)` (~line 868) with the translated body. `_estimate_prompt_tokens` (`lifecycle.py:224`) only counts `messages`, returns 0 for `input`-only bodies, so adaptive timeout collapses to base 60s (`60 + 0.015*0`), instead of ~1560s (capped to `upstream_request_timeout_seconds: 120`).
- Session recordings confirm proxy→provider bodies are `input`-only (`{'model','input','max_output_tokens','stream','tools'}`); a 406KB body should estimate ~100k tokens.
- Pool client read=300s and idle timeout 240s are NOT the source; the 60s httpx read timeout from the collapsed estimate is.
- User-visible effect: ~60s silence + 2s backoff + ~50s retry ≈ 110s apparent hang per tool-call turn; operator must nudge with "continue".
- Related: LP-0MTVPIO4O008V12K (empty-response retries), LP-0MTVPJWWZ000REYU (empty-response logging).

## Scope

Likely fix in `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` (`_estimate_prompt_tokens`) and/or `proxy/proxy/proxy_remote.py` (`proxy_to_remote`):

- Option A (preferred): teach `_estimate_prompt_tokens` to count Responses `input` items (text in `content`/`input_text` parts, `function_call`/`function_call_output` text) as well as chat `messages`.
- Option B: compute `remote_timeout` BEFORE `_translate_chat_to_responses` in `proxy_to_remote` (estimate on the original chat body).
- Consider promoting the computed adaptive timeout from `debug` to `info` (or at least including the estimate in the `[remote] POST` line) so future collapses are visible.
- Check non-streaming path (`_handle_remote_non_streaming`) uses the same estimator consistently.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

1. A Responses-shaped body with ~400KB of `input` text yields an adaptive timeout > 60s (capped by `upstream_request_timeout_seconds`), not the 60s base.
2. A chat-shaped body of the same size yields the same timeout as its translated Responses equivalent (parity).
3. Live/repro test: large-context opencode-go request no longer ReadTimeouts at exactly 60s; first-content arrival up to the capped timeout succeeds without Tier-1 retry.
4. Existing tests updated + new estimator cases added (chat body, Responses body, empty body); relevant proxy test suites pass.
data.title: Adaptive timeout ignores Responses input bodies, collapses to 60s ReadTimeout
